note: Old-growth redwood campground beside Elk Prairie at the south end of the Newton B. Drury Parkway; the two loops sit under the redwoods with Prairie Creek along their west side, and a few sites face the open prairie where Roosevelt elk graze. Trailers are limited to 24 ft; pads vary site to site. --Claude
summary: parks.ca.gov page + banner, campground map PDF, ReserveCalifornia (place/grid/details), Esri + OSM + 3DEP read. Open year-round; $35 all seasons and weekends; 61 bookable back-in sites 16-27 ft (35 take 23 ft+), motorhomes 27 / trailers 24 ft; no hookups, no dump; pay showers, water. Max stay 7 nights from mid-May, 30 off-season; sites 5-47 not on sale Dec-May. Creekside KEPT on the west rows (Prairie Creek ~20-30 m from the loop roads, 1-2 m drop). Pin fine.
flags: WATERFRONT creekside KEPT (hard check): the parks.ca.gov campground map draws Prairie Creek right along the west row of both loops - sites 26, 28, 29, 33, 35, 39, 40, 44, 45, 48 (north loop) and 50, 53, 55, 56, 57, 58, 60 (south loop); 43 is on the map but not an RC unit. Imagery is canopy-blind, so the evidence is OSM + 3DEP: the south loop's west road (41.35894,-124.03131) is 27 m from the creek line (41.35907,-124.03158) with a 32.5 -> 31.0 m drop, the north loop top (41.3601,-124.02911) 19 m from the creek (41.36026,-124.0292) with 34.8 -> 33.1 m - an easy wooded walk down with nothing between, within the creekside rule (2.2-2.75 m over a wooded slope passes). All are sold nightly on ReserveCalifornia; of those rows, 26, 33, 44, 45, 48, 55, 56 and 58 take 23 ft+. Prairie Creek is a small creek (well under 30 m), so creekside, not riverfront.
